chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) crucified a man at Al-Hira for three days, then brought him down on the fourth day, so he prayed over him and buried him.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.فَصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: So he prayed over him (performed funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: What did Amir al-Mu'minin do after crucifying a man for three days?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the practical application of the hadd of crucifixion (al-Salb) by Imam Ali (AS) in Al-Hira, illustrating the judicial discretion (ijtihad) of the Imam in determining the duration of the penalty. The subsequent prayer and burial signify the restoration of the individual's spiritual status and communal dignity after the execution of the punishment, reflecting the balance between justice and mercy in Shia jurisprudence. This event serves as a primary precedent for the classification of crucifixion as a distinct hadd penalty rather than merely a method of execution.
